traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 026.0-DEV-ELSE-IF-ANNOTATION-POSITION are satisfied:
- **Before-Else Position**: `gatherElseIfCommentText` and `gatherBranchCommentText` preserve existing behavior by first using ESLint’s `getCommentsBefore(node)`. The dedicated unit test `[REQ-DUAL-POSITION-DETECTION-ELSE-IF] detects annotations placed before the else-if keyword` verifies this. - **After-Condition Position & Fallback Logic**: For else-if branches with valid loc info, `scanElseIfBetweenConditionAndBody` and `scanElseIfInsideBlockComments` are used when no valid annotations exist before the else. The unit test `[REQ-FALLBACK-LOGIC-ELSE-IF] falls back to annotations between condition and body…` and the presence of an inside-block scan confirm both the fallback and multi-position detection. - **Position Priority**: `gatherElseIfCommentText` first checks preceding-line comments (`scanElseIfPrecedingComments`) and only falls back to between/inside when that contains no @story/@req. The `[REQ-POSITION-PRIORITY-ELSE-IF]` unit test shows that when both positions are annotated, only the before-else annotations are used. - **Auto-Fix Compatibility**: `getBranchAnnotationInfo` special-cases else-if branches with block consequents to set `insertPos` and `indent` to the first line inside the block body. The `[REQ-PRETTIER-AUTOFIX-ELSE-IF]` unit test confirms the fixer inserts at that line with correct inner indentation, which matches the documented Prettier-compatible placement. - **Prettier Compatibility**: The combined detection logic supports annotations before else-if, between condition and body, and inside the block, which covers how Prettier moves comments. The integration test file `tests/integration/else-if-annotation-prettier.integration.test.ts` uses real Prettier + ESLint to demonstrate that formatted code passes validation in both key scenarios; these tests are opt-in via an env flag but correctly exercise the behavior. - **No Regression**: The full Jest run (npm test) passes, including the extensive `require-branch-annotation` rule tests that cover many branch types, indicating other branch behaviors remain intact. - **Documentation**: `docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md` includes a clear, dedicated section describing valid else-if annotation positions, precedence, and auto-fix behavior, explicitly tied to the tests and this story.
Given the current code, tests, and documentation, this story is fully implemented and behaviorally validated.
